summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma on carfilzomib and revlimid, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and diastolic heart failure, was admitted for diarrhea, fatigue, and low-grade fever. Initial evaluation revealed dehydration, acute kidney injury likely pre-renal, and worsening anemia requiring a blood transfusion. His white blood cell count dropped to 1.0, prompting administration of filgrastim. Stool studies and imaging showed no infectious source; diarrhea was attributed to chemotherapy. Liver ultrasound revealed steatosis and gallstones without cholecystitis. He improved with supportive care, antibiotics were discontinued, and he was discharged home in stable condition with a new antihypertensive and close oncology follow-up.
